oracle_flags: RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 -Cpanic=abort --cfg rustc_oracle; the oracle links the provider object (--emit=link,obj); each generated provider is compiled to an object (--emit=obj)
development_note: the integrator approved the design notice and its four scope changes before this declaration. Exploration probes of the shapes (obj/parallel/auto-traits/reify/explore) ran against development builds before it. Every rustc, baseline, old-reader, forged-row, scaling, flip-survey and nonnull outcome was declared in scratch before the rustc oracle, the baseline probe and any candidate run of these frozen inputs; this file was frozen after the oracle and the baseline probe and before any candidate run. rustc 1.98.0 accepted all nine clients (exit 42, no warnings) and every generated provider but the two tracked ones, which needed the `panic_location` lang item for their reify shim; they gained the oracle-only `Location` that the panic-attributes and struct-constructors providers use, recorded before any candidate run of them, and then compiled. The notice's `make` returned `fn(&T) -> u8`; a reference parameter makes the target higher-ranked, which stays fenced, so `make` is `fn(T) -> u8` over `fn show(self)`
rule: approved design. Version-13 value code 23, `(23, [Value(item)])`, read as `ValueKind::Reify`, admitted only under the body-node profile. Its operand is a preceding code-16 Function value of `FunctionItem` type and its own type is a `Function` row; no coercion decision is serialized. Every consumer re-proves the item's applied signature (the template a direct call opens) against the pointer, as a client's own `let f: fn(..) = item;` requires: convention and variadicness equal, `unsafe` added but never removed, and the admitted closed Rust pointer domain binds no region, so interned parameter and result nodes compare exactly. A fn pointer over a type parameter is formed only conditionally, so its reification requests formation. Existing packets keep their bytes: export fenced code 23 before

cases.shape: `unsafe { base::as_unsafe()(7) }`: the safe item `hold` reified to `unsafe fn(u8) -> i32`; adding unsafe is allowed
`let f = base::erase::<u8>(); f(42u8) as i32`: `erase<T: Copy>` reifies `id::<T>` to `fn(T) -> T`, which requests its formation; the consumer instantiates it at u8
`base::getter()(base::W(42)) as i32`: the inherent method `W::get` reified to `fn(W) -> u8`

`base::make::<L>()(L) as i32` with a client `impl base::Show for L`: the const fn `make<T: Show>` reifies `<T as Show>::show` under a rigid `T`, shaped as `argument_new!`, and the consumer selects the client impl
`base::make::<u8>()(42u8) as i32`: the same const fn at a provider type, selecting the provider impl
`base::method()(41u8) as i32`: the trait method `<u8 as Tr>::f`, selected by the consumer, reified to `fn(u8) -> u8`
`let f = base::pick(); f(42u16) as i32`: the instance `id::<u16>` reified to `fn(u16) -> u16`
`unsafe { base::raw_ptr()(7) }`: the unsafe item `raw` reified to `unsafe fn(u8) -> i32`
`base::take()(7)`: a provider body returns the safe item `hold` as `fn(u8) -> i32`; the client calls the pointer locally

limits: closed Rust fn pointers only: higher-ranked and C targets keep their type-row fence until the anonymous callable item after 5b; argument_new!'s `fn(&T, &mut Formatter<'_>) -> Result` is that item's witness
